name: RansomwareAttack
description: A case template for handling suspected or confirmed ransomware incidents, including triage, containment, investigation, eradication, recovery, communications, and post-incident activities. Aligned to NIST SP 800-53r5 Incident Response controls (IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-8) and the ICS4ICS framework (ISA/IEC 62443, FEMA ICS, CISA guidance) for environments that include or may include operational technology (OT) or industrial control systems (ICS). ICS4ICS-specific guidance is annotated inline and can be disregarded where OT/ICS systems are not in scope.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership and stakeholders. Describe the nature of the incident, how and when it was detected, the estimated scope of impact, key findings, and current response status. Typically two to four paragraphs]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation. What was in-scope, what was explicitly excluded, and any limitations on access or evidence that constrained findings]**

## Analysis — MITRE ATT&CK® Framework

**[Map investigative findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework (https://attack.mitre.org) ]** 

**[Complete each subsection with specific techniques, evidence, and timeline data. Remove tactics where no activity was observed and note the absence explicitly]**

### TA0001 — Initial Access

**Techniques observed:** 

**[e.g. T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment, T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application]**

## Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Findings

**[Document CTI findings that provide context for the incident. Include threat actor attribution (if known or suspected), campaign associations, intelligence source references, and any correlations with known threat groups, malware families, or active campaigns]**

### Threat Actor Profile

**Suspected group / alias:** <!-- e.g. Wizard Spider / UNC1878 / Unknown -->

**Attribution confidence:** <!-- High / Moderate / Low / Unattributed -->

**Assessed motivation:** <!-- Financial / Espionage / Hacktivism / Unknown -->

**ATT&CK Group:** <!-- e.g. G0102 -->

**[Provide a narrative summary of the suspected or confirmed threat actor, including known aliases, affiliation, observed TTPs, and links to prior campaigns or public reporting]**

| Intelligence Source | Reference | Relevance |
|--------------------|-----------|----------|
| | | |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

**[Prioritised remediation actions to contain the incident, eradicate the threat, and prevent recurrence]**

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Isolate compromised systems and block confirmed IOCs at all network boundaries | | Critical | |
| 2 | Reset credentials for all affected and privileged accounts; enforce domain-wide reset if domain compromise confirmed | | Critical | |
| 3 | Preserve forensic evidence and engage legal counsel for regulatory notification obligations | | Critical | |
| 4 | Reimage compromised systems from trusted baselines and patch all exploited vulnerabilities | | High | |
| 5 | Deploy enhanced SIEM/EDR detection rules based on observed TTPs and IOCs | | High | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA across all remote access, email, and privileged accounts | Identity | High |
| 2 | Extend log retention to 12+ months with centralised, immutable storage | Logging | High |
| 3 | Conduct network segmentation review to limit lateral movement paths | Architecture | High |
| 4 | Implement offline / immutable backup strategy with regular restore validation | Resilience | High |
| 5 | Conduct tabletop exercises and red team assessments based on observed TTPs | Preparedness | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, overall impact, and the path forward. Suitable for sharing with executive leadership. Address overall attack chain from initial access to impact, threat actor sophistication, estimated dwell time, whether attribution is possible, and confidence in containment and recovery]**

tasks.title: Validate ransomware activity
tasks.description:
Confirm whether ransomware activity is present by identifying file encryption, ransom notes, destructive actions, service disruption, extortion messaging, or other supporting evidence. Determine whether the case is confirmed ransomware, attempted ransomware, suspicious activity, or a false positive.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Detection and analysis is the first phase of incident handling.

ICS4ICS: Notify the ICS/OT Team lead immediately if any OT assets, HMIs, historian servers, or engineering workstations are affected or suspected. Do not assume an IT-only scope until the OT environment has been explicitly assessed. Activate the Safety Officer if there is any possibility of physical process impact.

tasks.title: Activate ICS4ICS command structure and declare incident
tasks.description:
Declare the incident and activate the ICS4ICS command structure. Confirm the Incident Commander (IC) per the Delegation of Authority. Assign or confirm: Safety Officer (SOFR), Operations Section Chief, Planning Section Chief, Logistics Section Chief, Finance/Admin Section Chief, Public Information Officer (PIO), and Liaison Officer (LOFR). Notify the Crisis Management Team (CMT) — CEO, COO, CFO, CIO, Legal Counsel, and HES representative — per incident severity.

Conduct an ICS Form 201 (Incident Briefing) to establish shared situational awareness across the CIRT, ICS/OT Team, and IT Team. Begin the first operational period using the Planning P cycle.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Preparation is a defined phase of incident handling. IR-6 — Incident information must be reported to designated authorities within defined timeframes.

ICS4ICS: The IC holds Delegation of Authority and financial expenditure authority. If internal staffing cannot fill required roles, activate Mutual Aid agreements. Reference the ICS4ICS Delegation of Authority Template and ICS4ICS Mutual Aid Procedure Template.

tasks.title: Initiate incident communications and stakeholder notifications
tasks.description:
Notify required internal stakeholders and activate the appropriate incident response, management, legal, privacy, communications, and executive escalation paths based on case severity and business impact.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-6 — Personnel must report suspected incidents to the organizational IR capability within defined timeframes. IR-6(1) — Automated reporting mechanisms should be used where available. IR-7 — Incident response assistance resources must be made available to users.

ICS4ICS: The Public Information Officer (PIO) manages all external communications. The Liaison Officer (LOFR) coordinates with external agencies including CISA, sector ISACs, regulators, and law enforcement. All communications must flow through the ICS4ICS command structure — direct communication that bypasses the IC should be avoided during an active incident.

tasks.title: Identify affected systems, accounts, and business impact
tasks.description:
Determine the scope of the incident by identifying affected hosts, user accounts, servers, shares, applications, backup systems, and business functions. Document confirmed and suspected impact.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-5 — All incidents and affected systems must be tracked and documented. IR-4(a) — Accurate scope is required for containment and eradication. CM-8 — System component inventory must be used to validate scope.

ICS4ICS: Explicitly assess whether the incident has reached or could reach OT network segments. Identify affected or potentially affected assets by type: engineering workstations, HMIs, historian servers, PLCs, RTUs, DCS components, safety instrumented systems (SIS), and IT/OT boundary systems such as jump servers or data diodes. The Safety Officer must assess whether any process safety function has been impaired before operational decisions are made. Coordinate Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) for OT systems with the Business Continuity Planning (BCP) Team.

tasks.title: Preserve forensic evidence
tasks.description:
Collect and preserve volatile and non-volatile evidence from affected and suspected systems, including memory, disk artifacts, ransom notes, binaries, scripts, event logs, authentication logs, EDR telemetry, network telemetry, scheduled tasks, services, and persistence artifacts.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(12) — Forensic analysis of malicious code is a defined IR-4 enhancement. AU-9 — Audit log integrity must be preserved. AU-11 — Audit records must be retained for defined periods and protected from unauthorized modification.

ICS4ICS: Evidence collection from OT assets must be coordinated with the ICS/OT Team and, where required, the OEM or system integrator. Forensic procedures safe on IT systems may not be safe or feasible on live OT assets — always confirm with the ICS/OT Team before imaging or acquiring data from PLCs, RTUs, or DCS components. Preserve OT-specific artifacts: controller configuration backups, historian exports, network captures from OT segments, and HMI alarm and event logs.

tasks.title: Contain hosts, accounts, and network access
tasks.description:
Isolate affected or suspected systems, disable or restrict compromised accounts, revoke sessions, disable remote access paths as needed, and block malicious or suspicious infrastructure to prevent further spread.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Containment is a defined phase of incident handling. IR-4(2) — Dynamic reconfiguration of systems supports containment. AC-2 — Account management actions (disable, revoke) support containment. AC-17 — Remote access should be disabled or restricted as appropriate. SC-7 — Boundary protection controls should be leveraged for network-level containment.

ICS4ICS: CRITICAL — Isolating OT assets carries risk of physical process disruption. The Safety Officer must assess and approve all OT isolation actions before they are executed. Containment actions for OT systems must be coordinated with the ICS/OT Team and plant operations. Do not apply IT-standard isolation procedures to live OT systems without operational risk assessment. Document every OT containment action in the Incident Action Plan (IAP). Use ICS Form 215A (Incident Action Plan Safety Analysis) to formally record the safety risk assessment for proposed OT containment actions.

tasks.title: Develop and maintain the Incident Action Plan (IAP)
tasks.description:
Document and maintain the Incident Action Plan (IAP) for each operational period using the ICS4ICS Planning P cycle. The IAP defines incident objectives, tactical assignments, resource requirements, and safety considerations per operational period.

Complete for each operational period:
- ICS Form 202 (Incident Objectives) — overall objectives and commander's intent
- ICS Form 204 (Assignment List) — tactical assignments by section and branch
- ICS Form 215 (Operational Planning Worksheet) — resource and task coordination
- ICS Form 215A (IAP Safety Analysis) — safety risks for planned tactics, especially OT isolation or recovery actions

Brief all Section Chiefs before each operational period transition.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Incident handling must be consistent with the incident response plan. IR-8 — The incident response plan must address the structure and organization of the IR capability.

ICS4ICS: The Planning Section Chief owns the IAP. The IC approves it. The Planning P cycle keeps the response objectives-driven and prevents reactive, uncoordinated action.

tasks.title: Identify initial access vector
tasks.description:
Investigate how the threat actor gained access — phishing, exposed VPN, RDP, credential compromise, software vulnerability exploitation, malicious downloads, or third-party access.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Root cause analysis supports eradication and recurrence prevention. SI-3 — Malicious code protection controls should be assessed against the observed initial access method. RA-3 — Risk assessment findings inform the scope of the exploited vulnerability.

ICS4ICS: Assess whether the initial access vector provides or could have provided a path into OT network segments. Common OT-relevant vectors include: compromised vendor or contractor VPN credentials, phishing targeting OT operations staff, remote desktop access to engineering workstations, and exploitation of internet-exposed OT management interfaces. If vendor or third-party remote access is implicated, notify the Liaison Officer to coordinate vendor engagement.

tasks.title: Investigate privilege escalation and lateral movement
tasks.description:
Determine how the threat actor elevated privileges, moved through the environment, accessed additional systems, and expanded control across users, hosts, shares, or management infrastructure.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(4) — Information correlation across systems supports lateral movement analysis. IR-4(13) — Behavior analysis is a defined incident handling enhancement. AC-6 — Least privilege failures identified during investigation should be documented for post-incident remediation.

ICS4ICS: Explicitly determine whether lateral movement crossed the IT/OT boundary. Key pivot points include: OT jump servers or remote desktop gateways, historian servers with dual-network connectivity, shared domain accounts used across IT and OT, and vendor remote access paths. If the OT network was reached, escalate immediately to the IC and activate OT-specific containment procedures.

tasks.title: Assess data exfiltration and extortion risk
tasks.description:
Determine whether data was staged, compressed, transferred, or exposed prior to encryption. Identify sensitive data types, possible destinations, extortion indicators, and any leak-site or ransom communication references.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Exfiltration assessment is part of the analysis phase of incident handling. AU-6 — Audit log review and analysis supports detection of data staging and transfer. IR-6 — Confirmed or suspected exfiltration of regulated data may trigger mandatory reporting obligations.

ICS4ICS: Activate the ICS4ICS Ransomware Procedure. This pre-established procedure convenes the pre-authorized ransomware decision team — including Legal Counsel, CFO, and the IC — who hold authority over ransom payment decisions and associated legal and regulatory considerations. No contact with the threat actor should occur before this team is convened and OFAC sanctions screening has been completed. The Liaison Officer coordinates government reporting obligations via the ICS4ICS Government Reporting Procedure.

tasks.title: Analyze ransomware artifacts and behavior
tasks.description:
Analyze ransomware binaries, scripts, ransom notes, file extensions, process execution, command lines, persistence mechanisms, and related artifacts. Identify the ransomware family or variant if possible.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(12) — Malicious code and forensic analysis is a defined incident handling enhancement. SI-3 — Malicious code protection controls should be reviewed against the variant's observed evasion techniques.

ICS4ICS: Determine whether the ransomware variant has known OT or ICS-specific capabilities — including targeting of OT file types, ICS software installations, historian databases, or backup systems used in industrial environments. Search threat intelligence sources for prior reporting on this variant in OT contexts. Coordinate binary analysis with the ICS/OT Team if artifacts are found on OT-connected assets.

tasks.title: Extract, validate, and track IOCs
tasks.description:
Extract and validate indicators of compromise from malware artifacts, host evidence, network telemetry, and external intelligence sources. Add confirmed IOCs to the case, tag appropriately, and share with downstream systems as authorized.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(4) — IOC correlation with external organizations is a defined enhancement. IR-5 — Incidents and associated indicators must be tracked and documented. SI-4 — IOCs should be deployed into monitoring systems to detect related activity.

ICS4ICS: Share validated IOCs with sector ISACs and CISA as appropriate via the Liaison Officer. OT-specific IOCs — such as engineering workstation indicators, historian-targeted file hashes, or OT protocol anomalies — should be flagged separately for distribution to OT-focused intelligence communities.

tasks.title: Eradicate persistence and unauthorized access
tasks.description:
Remove malicious binaries, scripts, scheduled tasks, services, persistence mechanisms, unauthorized accounts, and attacker tools. Reset compromised credentials, revoke tokens, and remediate exposed services or exploited vulnerabilities.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Eradication is a defined phase of incident handling. IA-5 — Compromised credentials must be reset per authenticator management controls. CM-7 — Systems should be returned to a least-functionality baseline post-eradication. SI-2 — Exploited vulnerabilities must be remediated.

ICS4ICS: Eradication actions on OT systems must be approved by the Safety Officer and coordinated with the ICS/OT Team. Removing persistence from OT assets — including PLCs, RTUs, or DCS components — may require vendor engagement and a controlled maintenance window. Standard IT reimaging procedures must not be applied to OT assets without explicit ICS/OT Team confirmation. OT patch schedules must respect vendor support constraints and operational windows.

tasks.title: Validate backup integrity and recovery readiness
tasks.description:
Confirm that backups are clean, available, and uncompromised. Identify safe restore points and verify that containment, credential remediation, and persistence removal are complete before restoration begins.

NIST 800-53r5: CP-9 — System backup controls require that backups are conducted, protected, and regularly tested. CP-10 — System recovery and reconstitution requires systems be restored to a known state. IR-4(3) — Continuity of operations must be coordinated with contingency planning activities (CP-2).

ICS4ICS: Validate OT configuration backups separately from IT system backups. OT backup artifacts include: PLC and RTU logic, DCS and HMI project files, historian database backups, network configuration archives, and safety system parameter backups. Confirm these are stored offline or in a network-isolated location and predate the incident. The Disaster Recovery Planning (DRP) Team must confirm RPO/RTO alignment before recovery is authorized. The Safety Officer must confirm safety system integrity is validated before any OT recovery operation begins.

tasks.title: Restore systems and data
tasks.description:
Restore affected systems, services, and data from validated clean backups or rebuilt systems. Validate restored functionality, monitor for reinfection, and ensure all recovery actions are documented.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Recovery is a defined phase of incident handling. CP-10 — System recovery and reconstitution controls define how systems are restored to a known secure state. SI-4 — Enhanced monitoring must be applied to recovered systems to detect reinfection or residual attacker activity.

ICS4ICS: OT recovery must follow a staged, IC-approved process. Required steps before resuming automated control: confirm the OT network is clean and isolated from the threat; restore and validate OT configurations from offline backups; perform functional testing of control systems before reconnection to the process; obtain Safety Officer confirmation that safety system integrity is intact. The ICS/OT Team leads OT restoration. Vendor or OEM support must be arranged in advance through the Logistics Section Chief.

tasks.title: Assess external reporting and notification obligations
tasks.description:
Determine whether law enforcement, regulators, cyber insurance, customers, partners, or other external parties must be notified based on contractual, legal, regulatory, or policy requirements.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-6 — Incident information must be reported to designated organizational authorities within defined timeframes. IR-6(2) — Vulnerabilities associated with the incident should be reported to designated disclosure authorities.

ICS4ICS: Execute the ICS4ICS Government Reporting Procedure. This pre-established procedure defines the pre-authorized team and criteria for government reporting decisions. The Liaison Officer coordinates all external agency contacts including: CISA (888-282-0870 / report@cisa.gov), FBI / IC3, sector-specific regulators (e.g. NERC CIP for energy, TSA for pipelines and rail, NRC for nuclear, EPA for water/wastewater), sector ISACs, and the cyber insurer. The Finance/Admin Section Chief tracks all insurance notification deadlines and expenditures for claims purposes.

tasks.title: Harden controls and increase monitoring
tasks.description:
Implement security improvements identified during the investigation, including MFA enforcement, segmentation, credential hygiene, logging improvements, detection coverage, patching, backup protection, and monitoring enhancements.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Lessons from incident handling must be incorporated into IR procedures. SI-4 — System monitoring improvements should be applied based on observed TTPs. IA-2 — MFA enforcement addresses identity control gaps. AU-2 / AU-6 — Audit event coverage and log review should be enhanced based on gaps identified during the incident. SC-7 — Boundary protection improvements address lateral movement paths identified during investigation.

ICS4ICS: Hardening actions in OT environments must be change-managed through the ICS/OT Team and coordinated with vendor support constraints. Priority OT hardening actions: enforce MFA on all remote access paths to OT systems; review and restrict all IT/OT cross-segment connections; ensure OT network monitoring is in place across all zones; validate that OT configuration backup processes are tested and stored offline.

tasks.title: Conduct hotwash, lessons learned, and close case
tasks.description:
Lead an After-Action Review (Hotwash) to evaluate response performance against IAP objectives, capture lessons learned, and identify improvement actions. Confirm recovery is complete, no ongoing malicious activity is observed, required notifications are resolved, and closure criteria are met. Update the IR plan and ICS4ICS program based on findings.

NIST 800-53r5: IR-4(a) — Lessons learned from incident handling must be incorporated into IR procedures, training, and testing. IR-8 — The incident response plan must be updated based on lessons learned. IR-3 — IR testing and exercises must be updated to reflect observed TTPs and identified gaps.

ICS4ICS: The Hotwash is the final activity of the last operational period, led by the IC with all Section Chiefs and key responders. Evaluate: whether IAP objectives were met; effectiveness of each ICS4ICS role; coordination between CIRT, ICS/OT Team, and IT Team; and gaps in pre-incident procedures. Findings must feed back into the ICS4ICS program: updated Ransomware and Government Reporting Procedures, revised Job Aids, and improved exercise scenarios. The IC formally demobilizes the ICS structure and returns authority to normal operations.

> NIST 800-53r5: IR-4 — Incident handling phases: Preparation > Detection and Analysis > Containment > Eradication > Recovery.
> ICS4ICS: Response is structured around Planning P operational periods. Update the IAP (ICS Form 202) at each period boundary and brief all Section Chiefs before transitioning.

- [ ] Containment actioned; OT isolation safety-approved where applicable — IR-4, SC-7, ICS4ICS
- [ ] IAP completed for current operational period — ICS4ICS
- [ ] Root cause identified
- [ ] Persistence removed — CM-7
- [ ] Credentials remediated — IA-5
- [ ] OT safety system integrity confirmed before recovery — ICS4ICS
- [ ] Backup integrity validated — CP-9
- [ ] Recovery approved and in progress / complete — CP-10
- [ ] External notifications assessed and actioned — IR-6
- [ ] Government Reporting Procedure executed if required — ICS4ICS

notes.title: ICS4ICS command structure
notes.content:
## ICS4ICS Command Structure

> ICS4ICS applies the FEMA Incident Command System to OT/ICS cybersecurity incidents, separating technical cyber response from incident management so the right people are doing the right tasks. This structure applies even in IT-only ransomware incidents where OT scope has not been ruled out.

**Incident declared:** <!-- Yes / No -->
**Incident Commander (IC):** <!-- name -->
**Delegation of Authority confirmed:** <!-- Yes / No -->
**Mutual Aid activated:** <!-- Yes / No / N/A -->

---
